title: Leveraging IoT-Driven Customer Intelligence for Adaptive Financial Services
authors: Garg, A.; Mishra, S.; Jain, A.
venue: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, and Machine Learning
tldr: Proposes an IoT-driven layered architecture for personalized banking using real-time contextual data from wearables, ATMs, and mobile devices with AI analytics for adaptive financial services.
problem_and_motivation: Traditional banking relies on rigid product offerings and static personalization. IoT enables context-aware banking but faces challenges in data privacy, legacy system integration, and interoperability across fragmented device ecosystems.
approach: Uses hybrid methodology combining qualitative synthesis of academic and industrial sources with systems architecture modeling.
Designs a 5-layer architecture: Perception (IoT sensors), Network (5G/WiFi), Data Processing (real-time analytics), Service (personalized offers), and Feedback Loop.
Defines personalization scoring equation PScore_i = sum(w_j * x_ij) for service matching.
Reviews IoT use cases across global banking institutions including smart ATMs, wearables, geofencing, and voice banking.
Evaluates ROI benefits, security challenges, and implementation barriers.
findings: IoT in banking enables hyper-personalized services through real-time behavioral data from multiple touchpoints.
Key use cases include smart ATMs with biometrics, wearable-based payments, geofenced offers, and voice banking.
Data privacy, cybersecurity risks, and legacy system integration are primary adoption barriers.
Context-aware banking shifts from reactive to predictive service delivery.
ROI improvement through increased customer engagement and operational efficiency.
